title: Gemini 4 Neon
author: yigitdemirag
relevanceReason: 命中 3 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: Bringing frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows.

Gemini 4 Neon is available Delivers across enterprise, analytical, and scientific work Built for production-ready code Brings efficiency and control to production-grade workflows Built for fast, low cost, frontier-level cyber defense Designed for safe, dependable execution Built for deeper analysis Start building with Gemini 4 Neon today

Today, we’re introducing Gemini 4 Neon — bringing frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows.Neon ranks ahead of comparable models and #3 overall with a score of 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at its xhigh thinking level, landing just behind larger, slower models. On the Vals Index, Neon ranks #2 and lands on the Pareto frontier. Beyond just pushing on raw model capability, we’re continuing to make our models better to work with, Neon ranks #2 on steerability (adapting cleanly to mid-task user corrections) on the new Agent Arena Index. Neon also excels at multi-step instruction following and builds on our ongoing progress to curb fabrication, recording our lowest fabrication rate yet in internal Google Antigravity testing.The model is priced at $3 per million input tokens ($0.15 per million cached input tokens, a 95% discount) and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window.Gemini 4 Neon is rolling out today in the Gemini API in Google AI Studio, Gemini for business (via API and model dropdown), for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity, and for Pro and Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app.
summaryZh: Bringing frontier-level intelligence with fast end-to-end task completion across complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science workflows.

So if I am getting this right?

  +-------------------------------+--------------+--------+--------+----------+-------+
  |              Lab              |      XL      |   L    |   M+   |    M     | S/XS  |
  +-------------------------------+--------------+--------+--------+----------+-------+
  | Google (Gemini 4 Family #1)   |              | Argon  |        |          |       |
  | Google (Gemini 4 Family #2)   |              | Carbon | Neon   | Hydrogen |       |
  | Anthropic (Claude 5.2 Family) | Fable/Mythos |        |        |          |       |
  | Anthropic (Claude 5.5 Family) |              | Opus   |        | Sonnet   | Haiku |
  | OpenAI (GPT 6.2 Family)       | Astra        | Sol    |        |          |       |
  | OpenAI (GPT 6.1 Family)       |              |        |        | Terra    |       |
  | OpenAI (GPT 6 Family)         |              |        |        |          | Luna  |
  +-------------------------------+--------------+--------+--------+----------+-------+
Notes:

  * Gemini 4 Family
    - Argon   -- ++Train --> Carbon
    - Carbon  -- Distill --> Neon, Hydrogen
  * Gemini 3 Family
    - 3 Pro   -- ++Train --> 3.1 Pro
    - 3 Pro   -- Distill --> 3 Flash
    - 3 Flash -- ++Train --> 3.5 Flash ... -- ++Train --> ... 3.8 Flash
  * "S/XS" classification is due to weirdly low pricing for models by Ant/OAI and not by raw perf

children.author: locknitpicker
children.textRawHtml:
> I'm not sure it even makes sense to align models on price given that Neon appears to be considerably better than Sonnet/Terra.

Models are nowadays compared in terms of their position with regards to a Pareto front assessing traits such as capabilities and cost because there are clear tradeoffs between cost and capabilities.

I'm sure we are going to see speed show up in the analysis in the near future.

children.textRawHtml:
Only if you subscribe to all of them. Most people have one paid AI subscription with one provider so they have to learn ~four names for the models. Four is not good-lord-tier for the amount of value it brings. The thinking effort names are just regular English words.

Would you say the same about gadgets like oh my god I have to remember iPhone, iPad, iMac, MacBook pro and Air and Samsung Galaxy etc, or with gpus or with CPUs or with car brands or literally anything??
